```markdown
# Comprehensive sm_86 Live Data-Collection Campaign (RTX 3090 Ti) — Contract-First

## Goal Description

Scale the sm_86 ground-truth data-collection campaign from the 17-cell `portable_lcd` pilot to the **full sm_86-runnable roster** on the RTX 3090 Ti, producing the frozen corpus that M-SIM-1 and later simulator work consume: NCU labels (full metric vector), NVBit traces (the sim input), roster-wide SASS control-bits, calibration cards (pchase + new additive microbenches), per-metric repeatability/determinism floors, and a defensible typed-exclusion ledger.

The organizing principle is **contract-transition-first**: land the tracer ASYNC_COPY+ATOM address-exclusion flip as ONE fully-lockstepped, capability-versioned trace-contract transition (both flips in the same transition), keep the frozen campaign-M1 bundle as the pre-flip regression anchor, then capture the whole roster **exactly once** under the new address-carrying contract in immutable one-commit / one-roster / one-protocol / one-manifest chunks.

This is a **DATA-COLLECTION campaign only**. Building the M-SIM-1 eval-join, per-metric reporter, and baseline rigs is explicitly out of scope. No edits to existing validated code except (a) genuine bug fixes, (b) the sanctioned tracer flip plus its lockstep consumer widening, and (c) the sanctioned `freeze_label_bundle.py` widening (DEC-3); new files (roster JSONs, additive microbench probes, campaign-manifest + exclusion-ledger tools/schemas, supplemental-v3-only SOL shape-adjust wrappers after its pinned canary) are allowed.

## Current controlling state (2026-07-18)

ADRs 0001 and 0002 supersede older decision language in this plan. **Campaign**
M0–M3 are complete; campaign M4 is in progress; campaign M5 has not started;
campaign M6 and M7 are blocked. The canonical authority has 344 cells: 122
runnable, 222 excluded, and current defensible credit of 1/122 runnable. The
stopped 49-row revision and Task7/H3 capture-defect archive are zero-credit and
reuse-forbidden. The interrupted 53/201 SOL runnability attempt is separately
archived and canonical v1 is restored. Supplemental launch-set v3 is a separate
cohort and is live-disabled until a pinned canary passes; it cannot change
canonical campaign-M4/M7 accounting.

The three CUDA roles are independent and have no fallback: canonical C1
workloads use nvcc 13.3; supplemental SOL launch-set v3 uses nvcc 13.2; and the
NVBit/tracer artifact build independently uses nvcc 13.2. The supplemental role
remains live-disabled with its cohort until the pinned canary passes.

Task7/H3 continuation is authorized outside RLCR under the current live-campaign,
provenance, and hardware gates (`CONTINUE_PRESERVE_PINNED`). The sole
publication headline is `exec_cycles_gpc_max` / `gpc__cycles_elapsed.max`
(`CYCLES_ONLY_BINDING`): ≤10% MAPE meets the target, >10% and ≤15% is
floor-only, and >15% is publication failure. Cycles remain
`required_unimplemented` pending the checked-in aggregation-semantics study and
are operating-state- and protocol-bound, never claimed DVFS-stable. The seven
implemented simulator descriptors are reported secondary outputs and are
ungated.

The repeatability study supplies the noise floor used to interpret the cycles
accuracy gate and to contextualize the seven ungated secondary outputs. It does
not create a publication gate for a secondary metric or allow one to replace a
failed cycles headline. Archive-integrity, offline/frozen-hardware,
live-campaign, campaign-M7 completion, and M-SIM-1 are independent gates.

## Acceptance Criteria

The `AC-*` items describe the live-campaign completion contract outside RLCR.
All accuracy/coverage claims are against real-GPU NCU under the pinned protocol
v2.1; NCU values are targets/validation only and never enter model or card
inputs (Rule 1).

- AC-1: **Preflight, provenance foundation, and roster authority are established before any capture.** A preflight emitter records host + toolchain + clock state and gates capture; a machine-checkable roster authority enumerates the universe, the runnable set, and the excluded set. Canonical campaign accounting continues to consume restored historical SOL runnability v1. Any fresh SOL reconstitution, shrink, or runnable-count work described below belongs only to the separate supplemental-v3 cohort and remains live-disabled pending its pinned canary; it does not mutate canonical v1.
  - Positive Tests (expected to PASS):
    - Preflight manifest records git HEAD, `working_tree_clean`, NCU/driver/canonical-workload-nvcc/NVBit versions matching the capture pins (NCU 2026.1.0 / driver 610.43.02 / canonical C1 CUDA 13.3 nvcc / NVBit 1.8), separately verifies supplemental SOL launch-set v3's CUDA 13.2 nvcc pin (without enabling live v3 work), separately verifies the independent CUDA 13.2 nvcc used for NVBit/tracer and static-rebind build provenance, clocks == v2.1 (core 1350 / mem 10501, persistence on), a `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=.toolchain/pb/lib` injection smoke that yields a nonzero contract-valid trace, and declared free disk > the authored trace-retention budget.
    - The roster authority manifest resolves to a total universe count, a runnable-set count, and an excluded-set count with `universe == runnable + excluded`, each row carrying `roster_source`, binary, app-args, shape selector, and sha256 pins.
  - Negative Tests (expected to FAIL):
    - A dirty unrecorded worktree, unlocked host clocks for the reference config, a missing `.toolchain/pb` runtime, or a missing trace-budget file causes preflight to fail BEFORE any capture runs.
    - A roster authority where any runnable cell lacks a resolvable binary/shape/app-args, or where `universe != runnable + excluded`, fails.

- **Supplemental-v3 contract — outside AC-1 and canonical campaign-M4/M7; live-disabled until its pinned canary passes.** It cannot gate, expand, or mutate canonical v1.
  - Positive test after canary authorization: SOL-ExecBench reconstitution reproduces a separate runnable/deferred split on this host (data via `download_data.sh`, environment via `uv sync`, CUTLASS via `CUTLASS_DIR` override) fingerprinted by a native-env hash; each of the 23 historical OOM cells is first re-checked under `--replay-mode application`, then, only if still needed, shrunk per `plans/sm86_sol_shrink_to_fit_fable5_answer.md` with full native-shape and regime provenance.
  - Negative tests after canary authorization: a `shape_adjusted` cell lacking its native-shape reference or typed failure reason fails; a shrink that cuts attention B·H below CTA saturation without a regime flag fails; a cell whose post-capture `dram__bytes.sum` deviates > ±30% from its footprint model without demotion to `reduced_representative` fails.

- AC-2: **The frozen campaign-M1 bundle is a green pre-flip regression anchor.** `eval/frozen_labels/sm86_m1_bundle_v21.json` validates and replays under old-contract semantics, byte-identical, before the flip.
  - Positive Tests: replay/validate the frozen bundle → 15 admitted / 2 typed-excluded cells; `smsp__inst_executed.sum` EXACT 15/15; L1 op_ld sector-hit-rate label-exact; all bundle sha256 pins reproduce.
  - Negative Tests: any new validation failure, changed admitted/excluded count, or sha256 mismatch on the frozen bundle fails (guards against accidental pre-flip drift or a premature contract change).

- AC-3: **The tracer trace-contract transition lands as ONE lockstepped, capability-versioned commit with consumer widening and synthetic tests — semantically correct for atomics vs async-copy, with BOTH flips included.**
  - AC-3.1: The producer flip stops the host-side drop of the addressed classes and stamps a manifest-level `trace_contract_id` plus a producer capability list (`memory_payload_classes`); the SASS classifier is untouched; the proto is regenerated and re-pinned in the same commit.
  - AC-3.2: Consumers are widened in lockstep to ENFORCE identity, not merely decode the enum: `import_trace_contract` extends its global-class allocation-identity gate to address-bearing atomic/async-copy records; `tools/sector_stream/generator.py`, HRD, `order_projections`, and the cache-access policy are aligned to the new payload classes; the Rust `sim/trace` reader enforces the same identity the Python gate does.
  - AC-3.3: Synthetic producer fixtures cover ordinary global load, **global atomic**, **shared atomic (ATOMS)**, **RED**, **LDGSTS (cp.async)**, and predicated-off memory records. The ATOMIC flip was implemented and tested first WITHIN this single contract transition; the ASYNC_COPY (LDGSTS) flip was adjudicated (source/destination operand semantics proven), widened, tested, and included in the SAME contract transition before the transition completed. "Atomic-first" was an internal implementation ordering only — never "atomic-only now, async later"; campaign M2 did not complete and full-roster capture (AC-5) did not start until BOTH flips were in the contract.
  - Positive Tests: a new-contract trace with an active global atomic or LDGSTS-source record carries `allocation_id` + `memory_op_class` + `data_width`; a shared-atomic (ATOMS) record is classified without being forced through the global allocation-id rule; the frozen campaign-M1 traces still validate with the capability absent.
  - Negative Tests: a new-contract active global-atomic / LDGSTS-source record with `allocation_id` absent or zero is REJECTED; forcing a shared atomic through global allocation identity is REJECTED; a `.proto` change committed without its pin regeneration fails `cargo test`.

- AC-4: **A new-contract canary proves the flip unlocked scorability without regressing exact metrics.** A small canary set (ordinary load, global atomic, shared-atomic/RED, LDGSTS) is captured under the new contract.
  - Positive Tests: the canary manifest shows the new `trace_contract_id` + capability list, nonzero admitted atomic/async records where expected, and no unexpected `unsupported_memory_path` rows; a previously-`na` tensor-core op_ld cell (e.g. `gemm_hmma_bf16`) and the atomic histogram L2 cell become scorable; `smsp__inst_executed.sum` and L1 op_ld exactness on the pre-existing cells are unchanged.
  - Negative Tests: a canary cell that still emits address-stripped `unsupported_memory_path` for the flipped classes fails; any regression in `smsp__inst_executed.sum` or L1 op_ld exactness on the pre-existing cells fails.

- AC-5: **The full runnable roster is captured once under the new contract at the v2.1 reference protocol** — traces + full-metric-vector labels + control-bits — with resume/idempotence, per-chunk provenance, and typed sampling for budget-breaching cells.
  - Positive Tests: for every runnable cell, admitted outputs contain a full-registry NCU label sidecar (the sm_86-available metric set), a contract-valid NVBit trace, a control-bits sidecar, a binary-sha256 join, and a v2.1 protocol stamp; the roster-authority count equals admitted + typed-excluded; re-running a completed chunk skips cells whose sidecar hashes already match; each immutable chunk emits a DONE-manifest (command, source_commit, dirty-state, tool versions, protocol, roster hash, budget hash, output root, pass/fail counts, typed-failure rows) and passes a pre/post source-commit equality check; a cell that breaches the trace budget is handled per the AC-9 sampling ladder (compression-first, admissibility-gated, wave-segment/reduced-shape, typed) — never silently truncated.
  - Negative Tests: any runnable cell present in NEITHER admitted outputs NOR the exclusion ledger fails the phase; a cell whose repeats span differing `source_commit` (mid-sweep commit → `label_provenance_duplicate`) fails; a budget-breaching cell captured without the AC-9 sampling ladder and its typed provenance fails; an incomplete trace (block coverage < 100% vs the launch `gridDim`) accepted without a `trace_sampling` sidecar fails.

- AC-6: **Calibration cards are refreshed/extended from the Fable-5-designed six-probe clock64 suite, Rule-1 clean, overdetermined, and stored as additive evidence in the current campaign scope** (designs: `plans/sm86_calibration_microbench_design_fable5_answer.md` for (a)–(e) + `plans/sm86_cp_async_timing_probe_fable5_answer.md` for (f)). pchase is re-run under the lock; the suite is built in **load-bearing order (b) port-width → (f) cp.async/LDGSTS timing → (a) L2↔DRAM fetch-granularity → (d) MSHR/MLP saturation → (c) achievable DRAM bandwidth → (e) L2 associativity/slice-hash**, at **execution order b, a, d, f, c, e** (f consumes (b)'s port + (d)'s MSHR verdicts, so it runs after both); (b)+(d) run as a Little's-law-coupled pair, and (f) = the F-L completion-latency + F-T streaming-plateau + F-B burst-issue sub-probes; control-bits are extended roster-wide. The sim `LDGSTS` event-model that consumes (f)'s constants (f1–f5) and the read-only attribution pass that confirms (f)'s provisional rank are downstream (FUT-6).
  - Positive Tests: each probe emits a measured value OR a typed bounded gap from the taxonomy {`RANGE`, `CENSORED`, `MIXTURE`, `UNRESOLVED_STRUCTURE`, `SURFACE_GAP`} carrying its full evidence curve + in-run positive/negative controls + confound verdicts, written as ADDITIVE evidence files (not transcribed into the byte-pinned `arch_profiles/cards/sm_86.json` in the current campaign scope, per DEC-3); every card constant is **overdetermined by ≥ 2 independent probe readouts that must agree under the hardware hypothesis** (Little's-law triangulation (b)×(d), RTT-contrast, persistence/Δ-contrast); control-bits sidecars exist for every runnable binary (0 unknown_encoding, or typed); a Rule-1 guard proves no NCU metric entered any card-input derivation.
  - Negative Tests: any card input traceable to an NCU metric fails the Rule-1 guard; a microbench that produces neither a value nor a typed bounded gap (a silent guess) fails; a card constant derived from a SINGLE readout or tuned against the simulator's end-to-end output fails the overdetermination rule (cross-probe contradictions are recorded as typed contradictions, never averaged away); an edit to `arch_profiles/cards/sm_86.json` transcribing a microbench value in the current campaign scope fails the DEC-3 boundary check.

- AC-7: **The full cross-protocol repeatability matrix is captured and analyzed by the Fable-5 uncensored determinism-study design** (full design: `plans/sm86_determinism_study_stats_fable5_answer.md`). Cells × {clock none/base/boost} × {cache all/none}, at **N=20 for the reference config (`clock=none`×`cache=all`) / N=10 for the five non-reference configs / escalate the reference to N=30** on a pre-registered trigger (modality/outlier flag, boundary-proximity, any out-of-range repeat, discrete-with-≥2-values); repeats collected as R shuffled sweeps, one fresh process per profile.
  - Positive Tests: the accounting identity `collected == classified + excluded_typed` holds and the study reproduces the historical admission set bit-for-bit via the imported `dispersion_gate` (the admission gate is demoted to a `would_have_been_admitted` reporting flag, not a filter); a NAMED uncensored `determinism_study` artifact (distinct from the admitted-only `matrix_summary.json`) classifies every `(cell,metric,config)` into the priority-ordered taxonomy {`out_of_range`/`vendor_defect`, `insufficient_evidence`, `multimodal`, `deterministic`, `quasi_stable`, `clock_noise`, `noisy`, `unstable`} via `sigma_rel` (d₂(N)-normalized for range rules, unit-asserted); pct-overflow rows are retained-typed (`ncu_pct_overflow`, never clamped/imputed) with per-(metric,config) OOR rate reported and the host-locked reference confirmed r=0; the two-stage small-N modality detector flags at tier-1 and certifies only at N=30; accuracy-gate denominators are the pooled P90 floor + per-cell override with the per-class rules; cross-protocol sensitivity is reported on the two SEPARATE axes (clock=instrument / cache=state) by equivalence testing; a cost/resume gate lets the sweep stop and resume without recomputing completed chunks.
  - Negative Tests: any admitted row produced by clipping or normalizing an out-of-range NCU percentage fails; an adaptive stop-when-CV-stable rule used for N (optional-stopping bias) fails; back-to-back same-process (non-shuffled) repeat collection fails the run-order design; a cell dropped without a typed exclusion reason (breaking the accounting identity) fails; a single-support outlier classified as `multimodal` fails; the classification statistic diverging from the imported `dispersion_gate` (a re-introduced scale bug) fails the lockstep property test.

- AC-8: **The full-roster corpus is frozen with a complete, defensible provenance and exclusion ledger.**
  - Positive Tests: the sanctioned widened freezer (DEC-3) emits, per admitted cell, every sm_86-available registered metric (mean + dispersion + repeatability rule), plus trace/control-bit/card-evidence manifests, source/protocol/tool hashes, and the `trace_contract_id`; a single typed-exclusion authority ledger classifies every non-captured cell with a reason ∈ {`arch_gate`, `semantic_mismatch`, `trace_unsupported`, `repeatability_failed`, `correctness_failed`, `calibration_inconclusive`, `host_capacity_deferred`} and satisfies `denominator == universe − Σ(typed exclusions)`; `shape_adjusted` is recorded as capture provenance on runnable cells, never as an exclusion reason; the freezer's `binary_sha256` check uses equality (the substring-idiom bug is fixed); the frozen bundle reports zero unresolved `problems`.
  - Negative Tests: a bundle with a cell in neither admitted outputs nor the ledger fails; a ledger row with a null/undefined `typed_reason` fails; a freezer that admits a cell whose label and trace `binary_sha256` differ (but one contains the other as a substring) fails.

- AC-9: **Trace-sampling for budget-breaching cells is compression-first, gate-routed, honest-by-construction, and golden-set-validated** (detailed design: `plans/sm86_trace_sampling_strategy_fable5_design.md`).
  - Positive Tests: lossless zstd compression + a compressibility probe are applied FIRST (contract hashes over decompressed bytes) and clear every cell that fits after compression; each still-breaching cell is routed by a deterministic admissibility-gate classifier (`coop_gate`/`wave_gate`/`atomic_gate`/`skew_gate`/`homogeneity`) to exactly one typed method with recorded gate verdicts; a wave-segment stratified-subset cell carries a valid closed-schema `trace_sampling.json` sidecar (method, gates, wave_model, strata, selected block IDs, estimator mode, `not_recoverable` list, `label_pairing`, tracer/stats-version pins) and HT calibrated-ratio estimates with stratified-cluster-bootstrap CIs meeting the stopping rule (rates ≤ 0.02 absolute half-width, counts ≤ 5% relative, ≥ 8 sampled segments, calibration self-check `X̂ ≈ X` within CI); the `sim/trace` reader fail-closes on an incomplete trace lacking a sidecar (`E_INCOMPLETE_TRACE`) and rejects a subset that rewrote `gridDim` (cross-checking the launch record against the sidecar `original_grid`); a golden-set fidelity run (8–12 small cells, full-vs-sampled at fractions × seeds) passes accuracy (p95 |R̂−R| ≤ 0.02 rates, ≤ 5% counts), CI coverage ≥ 90%, and sampling-induced error ≤ 0.3× the model MAE, WITH the histogram + few-wave negative controls correctly FAILING / gate-forbidden.
  - Negative Tests: a block-subset applied to a cell that fails `coop_gate`/`wave_gate`/`atomic_gate` is accepted (must FAIL — it must route to reduced-shape or `unavailable`); an incomplete trace accepted without a sidecar (must FAIL); cycles emitted as an exact full-shape prediction from a sampled trace (must FAIL — cycles are `not_recoverable`); a `dataset_shrunk` reduced-shape whose working set drops below the 6 MB L2 without the typed footprint flag (must FAIL); per-record or deterministic every-k decimation used as a sampling method (must FAIL — inadmissible); the golden-set negative controls PASSING, i.e. the estimator certifies a histogram-class cell (must FAIL the validation).

## Path Boundaries

### Upper Bound (Maximum Acceptable Scope)
The restored canonical-v1 authority — 344 cells, with 122 runnable and 222 excluded — is the sole campaign-M4/M7 cohort. Its runnable cells are captured once under the new address-carrying contract with the full sm_86-available NCU metric vector, the complete 6-config × N-repeat cross-protocol repeatability matrix, all three additive microbenches resolved (or typed-bounded), BOTH the ATOMIC and ASYNC_COPY flips landed and lockstep-verified in one contract transition, the pchase card refreshed as additive evidence, control-bits roster-wide, and a frozen corpus whose typed-exclusion authority ledger accounts for every non-captured cell. Budget-breaching cells are handled by the compression-first ladder (AC-9) — wave-segment subset only where the admissibility gates pass, reduced-shape or typed `unavailable` otherwise, with golden-set-validated estimators and negative controls. Fresh SOL reconstitution, shrink, or runnable-count work is excluded from this bound and belongs only to live-disabled supplemental v3.

### Lower Bound (Minimum Acceptable Scope)
The same restored canonical-v1 cohort, with typed records only where hardware genuinely blocks: both flips landed and canary-verified in the single contract transition; every canonical runnable cell either captured or assigned an authorized typed outcome; at least the reference-config full-metric capture banked for every runnable cell before the expensive protocol cross-product; microbenches that stay inconclusive recorded as typed bounded gaps; budget-breaching cells handled by the AC-9 compression-first ladder (at minimum: compression + the admissibility gate + the `sim/trace` reader fail-closed + typed `unavailable`/reduced-shape for gate-forbidden cells; the full wave-segment estimator + golden-set validation may narrow to the minority of cells that still breach after compression). At BOTH bounds the honest denominator, per-chunk provenance, the pre-flip regression anchor, and the typed-exclusion ledger are non-negotiable. Supplemental-v3 cells cannot satisfy or expand this lower bound.

### Allowed Choices
- Can use: existing roster-generator/adaptor sources (verification only; not authority to rewrite canonical v1); new additive microbench `.cu`/`.py` probes; new campaign-manifest emitter + typed-exclusion authority ledger + their schemas; SOL shape-adjust wrappers only inside supplemental v3 after its pinned canary; the sanctioned tracer flip + lockstep consumer widening; the sanctioned `freeze_label_bundle.py` widening (DEC-3); genuine bug fixes (e.g. the freezer substring-vs-equality `binary_sha256` idiom); supplemental-v3 SOL environment reconstitution (only after its pinned canary, never for canonical campaign M4) via env overrides / shims (`CUTLASS_DIR`, path-remap) + `uv sync` + HF `download_data.sh`; resume/idempotence wrappers around the existing runners; the AC-9 trace-sampling ladder for budget-breaching cells (zstd compression tier + `.pb.zst` + the compressibility probe, the admissibility-gate classifier, two-pass counting/dump capture, the wave-segment HT estimator, and the closed-schema `trace_sampling.json` sidecar); the `sim/trace` reader completeness fail-closed (a genuine bug fix — closes the silent-incomplete-trace hole) + the never-rewrite-`gridDim` cross-check.
- Cannot use: NCU values as model or card inputs (Rule 1); edits to existing validated code beyond genuine bug fixes, the sanctioned flip, and the sanctioned freezer widening; editing the byte-pinned `arch_profiles/cards/sm_86.json` to transcribe calibration values in the current campaign scope (DEC-3 — stays additive evidence, transcribed under a separate approved change); normalizing/clipping pct-overflow into admitted labels; committing while a capture sweep is running; capturing degenerate-fallback simbench kernels (arch-gated kernels forced to sm_86) as calibration or gate data; silent (untyped) trace truncation; per-record or deterministic every-k trace decimation (inadmissible — breaks ordered replay); block-subset sampling of `coop_gate`/`wave_gate`/`atomic_gate`-forbidden cells; emitting cycles as an exact full-shape prediction from a sampled trace; a `dataset_shrunk` reduced-shape that drops the working set below the 6 MB L2 without the typed footprint flag; building the M-SIM-1 eval-join / reporter / baseline rigs and the typed scoring-side guard (out of scope; FUT-1 / FUT-5).

## Feasibility Hints and Suggestions

### Conceptual Approach
Sequence the campaign so the denominator is knowable before the expensive work and the contract is stable before capture:
1. Canonical preflight + authorities: reassert clock locks; record host/toolchain; build the campaign-manifest emitter, roster-authority generator, and typed-exclusion ledger skeleton; author the trace-retention budget + sampling strategy; bind the restored canonical-v1 344/122/222 authority. Do not run or wait on supplemental-v3 SOL reconstitution/shrink; it remains live-disabled pending its pinned canary.
2. Anchor: replay the frozen campaign-M1 bundle under old-contract semantics; assert byte-identity.
3. Flip (under the current source, provenance, and offline gates): land the producer capability bump + `trace_contract_id`, widen the identity-enforcing consumers in lockstep, add synthetic fixtures; atomic implemented first, async-copy adjudicated and included in the SAME transition.
4. Canary: capture a handful of new-contract cells spanning load/atomic/RED/LDGSTS; prove scorability unlocked and exact metrics unchanged.
5. Reference capture: consume the byte-exact restored canonical-v1 roster; do not regenerate or replace its matrix during cleanup. Run reference-config full-registry capture (traces + labels + control-bits) in immutable, resumable chunks with DONE-manifests; apply the AC-9 compression-first ladder to budget-breaching cells (compress + probe first; gate-classify; wave-segment subset / reduced-shape / typed unavailable).
6. Calibration: pchase re-run + three additive clock64 probes + MSHR/L2-assoc rerun-or-bound + roster-wide control-bits; store as additive evidence, Rule-1 guarded.
7. Matrix: run the full cross-protocol repeatability sweep with a cost/resume gate; emit the uncensored dispersion artifact + determinism classes; type pct-overflow.
8. Freeze: widen the freezer to the full metric vector; emit the frozen bundle + all manifests + the exclusion authority ledger; assert the denominator identity.

## Dependencies and Sequence

### Campaign milestones (M0–M7; distinct from M-SIM-1)
1. **M0 — Preflight & Authorities — complete**: preflight/provenance emitter; roster-authority generator; exclusion-ledger skeleton; trace-retention budget + sampling strategy; canonical runnability authority.
   - Phase A: host/toolchain/clock reassert + record; injection smoke; disk budget.
   - Phase B: roster authority (universe/runnable/excluded) + canonical runnability binding.
2. **M1 — Pre-flip Anchor — complete**: replay + byte-identity assert of the frozen M1 bundle. Depends on M0-A.
3. **M2 — Contract Transition — complete**: producer flip (both classes) + capability/`trace_contract_id` + proto repin + lockstep consumer widening + synthetic fixtures; atomic implemented first, async-copy after operand adjudication, both in one transition. Depends on M1. This is campaign M2, not M-SIM-1.
4. **M3 — Canary — complete**: new-contract capture across load/atomic/RED/LDGSTS; scorability + no-regression proof. Depends on campaign M2.
5. **M4 — Reference Capture — in progress**: consume the byte-exact restored canonical-v1 roster + run reference-config full-registry capture (traces+labels+control-bits) in resumable chunks; typed sampling for oversized cells. Depends on M0-B, M3. Do not regenerate or replace the frozen canonical matrix during cleanup.
6. **M5 — Calibration — not started**: pchase re-run + additive probes + MSHR/L2-assoc + roster-wide control-bits, Rule-1 guarded, additive-only. Depends on M0-A.
7. **M6 — Repeatability Matrix — blocked on M4**: full cross-protocol sweep + uncensored dispersion + determinism classes + cost/resume gate.
8. **M7 — Freeze — blocked on M4, M5, and M6**: widened freezer + frozen bundle + exclusion authority ledger + denominator identity.
```

### E718 | sources: static-registry-projection, causal-schedule-transaction-a-b, science-cost-and-handoff-b | supports: B702, B704, B712, B714, B715
<!-- FABLE5-EVIDENCE
{"excerpt_sha256":"6363436b671d50583e83e034277cb3b110edf9213c75ab5dd0536bde49445209","file_sha256":"6363436b671d50583e83e034277cb3b110edf9213c75ab5dd0536bde49445209","file_total_lines":372,"final_newline":true,"full_required_justification":"All numerical domain checks, summaries, classifications, floor bounds, and tests interact in one compact module.","id":"E718","kind":"file_full","lines":[1,372],"non_operational":true,"path":"tools/local_labels/m6_determinism_stats.py","revision":"WORKTREE","role":"decision","selection_reason":"The complete M6 statistics module defines finite/OOR validation, robust summaries, floors, denominators, and sensitivity inputs whose scientific nonvacuity and covariate ancestry must be closed.","supports":["B702","B704","B712","B714","B715"]}

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Shared, uncensored dispersion and classification primitives for M6."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
import random
import statistics
from dataclasses import dataclass
from statistics import NormalDist
from typing import Sequence

D2_EXACT = {5: 2.326, 10: 3.078, 20: 3.735, 30: 4.086}
CLASS_BOUNDARIES = (0.005, 0.02, 0.10)
DETERMINISM_CLASSES = (
    "vendor_defect",
    "insufficient_evidence",
    "multimodal",
    "deterministic",
    "quasi_stable",
    "clock_noise",
    "noisy",
    "unstable",
)


class DispersionError(ValueError):
    """A dispersion input violates the finite numeric contract."""


def _values(values: Sequence[float | int]) -> list[float]:
    out: list[float] = []
    for value in values:
        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
            raise DispersionError("values must be JSON numbers, not booleans")
        value = float(value)
        if not math.isfinite(value):
            raise DispersionError("values must be finite")
        out.append(value)
    return out


def dispersion_gate(rule: str, values: Sequence[float | int]) -> float | None:
    """Return the historical admission statistic without classification transforms."""

    vals = _values(values)
    if len(vals) < 2:
        return None
    mean = statistics.fmean(vals)
    if rule == "stddev_abs":
        return statistics.stdev(vals)
    if rule == "coefficient_of_variation":
        spread = statistics.stdev(vals)
        if mean == 0:
            return 0.0 if spread == 0 else None
        return spread / abs(mean)
    if rule == "relative_tolerance":
        spread = max(vals) - min(vals)
        if spread == 0:
            return 0.0
        if mean == 0:
            return None
        return spread / abs(mean)
    raise DispersionError(f"unknown repeatability rule: {rule}")


def d2_for_n(n: int) -> float:
    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 2:
        raise DispersionError("d2 requires integer N >= 2")
    if n in D2_EXACT:
        return D2_EXACT[n]
    # Blom order-statistic approximation. The four campaign tier values above
    # remain exact constants; this branch handles OOR-reduced sample counts.
    p = (n - 0.375) / (n + 0.25)
    return 2.0 * NormalDist().inv_cdf(p)


def sigma_rel(
    rule: str,
    values: Sequence[float | int],
    *,
    absolute_resolution: float = 0.0,
) -> float | None:
    """Map all registered repeatability rules to a common sigma-relative scale."""

    vals = _values(values)
    if len(vals) < 2:
        return None
    if max(vals) == min(vals):
        return 0.0
    mean = statistics.fmean(vals)
    denominator = abs(mean)
    if denominator < absolute_resolution:
        denominator = absolute_resolution
    if denominator == 0:
        return None
    if rule in {"stddev_abs", "coefficient_of_variation"}:
        return statistics.stdev(vals) / denominator
    if rule == "relative_tolerance":
        return (max(vals) - min(vals)) / (d2_for_n(len(vals)) * denominator)
    raise DispersionError(f"unknown repeatability rule: {rule}")


def c4(n: int) -> float:
    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 2:
        raise DispersionError("c4 requires integer N >= 2")
    return math.exp(
        0.5 * math.log(2.0 / (n - 1))
        + math.lgamma(n / 2.0)
        - math.lgamma((n - 1) / 2.0)
    )


def sigma_upper_factor(n: int, confidence: float = 0.95) -> float:
    """One-sided sigma upper factor using the Wilson-Hilferty chi-square quantile."""

    if isinstance(n, bool) or not isinstance(n, int) or n < 2:
        raise DispersionError("sigma upper factor requires integer N >= 2")
    if not 0.5 < confidence < 1.0:
        raise DispersionError("confidence must be in (0.5,1)")
    degrees = n - 1
    z = NormalDist().inv_cdf(1.0 - confidence)
    base = 1.0 - 2.0 / (9.0 * degrees) + z * math.sqrt(2.0 / (9.0 * degrees))
    if base <= 0:
        return float("inf")
    chi_lower = degrees * base**3
    return math.sqrt(degrees / chi_lower)


def classify_sigma(value: float | None, values: Sequence[float | int]) -> str:
    vals = _values(values)
    if len(vals) < 5 or value is None:
        return "insufficient_evidence"
    if max(vals) == min(vals):
        return "deterministic"
    if value <= CLASS_BOUNDARIES[0]:
        return "quasi_stable"
    if value <= CLASS_BOUNDARIES[1]:
        return "clock_noise"
    if value <= CLASS_BOUNDARIES[2]:
        return "noisy"
    return "unstable"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModalityResult:
    flagged: bool
    outlier_flag: bool
    certified: bool
    suspected: bool
    split_index: int | None
    gap: float | None
    reason: str | None


def _continuous_delta_bic(values: Sequence[float], split_index: int, variance_floor: float) -> float:
    """Return BIC(single Gaussian) - BIC(two-component Gaussian mixture)."""

    vals = [float(value) for value in values]
    n = len(vals)
    floor = max(float(variance_floor) ** 2, 1e-30)

    def gaussian_logpdf(value: float, mean: float, variance: float) -> float:
        variance = max(variance, floor)
        return -0.5 * (math.log(2.0 * math.pi * variance) + (value - mean) ** 2 / variance)

    mean_one = statistics.fmean(vals)
    variance_one = max(statistics.fmean((value - mean_one) ** 2 for value in vals), floor)
    loglike_one = sum(gaussian_logpdf(value, mean_one, variance_one) for value in vals)

    left = vals[:split_index]
    right = vals[split_index:]
    weights = [len(left) / n, len(right) / n]
    means = [statistics.fmean(left), statistics.fmean(right)]
    variances = [
        max(statistics.fmean((value - means[index]) ** 2 for value in group), floor)
        for index, group in enumerate((left, right))
    ]
    loglike_two = float("-inf")
    for _ in range(100):
        responsibilities: list[tuple[float, float]] = []
        next_loglike = 0.0
        for value in vals:
            logs = [
                math.log(max(weights[index], 1e-12))
                + gaussian_logpdf(value, means[index], variances[index])
                for index in (0, 1)
            ]
            pivot = max(logs)
            total = math.exp(logs[0] - pivot) + math.exp(logs[1] - pivot)
            next_loglike += pivot + math.log(total)
            responsibilities.append(
                (math.exp(logs[0] - pivot) / total, math.exp(logs[1] - pivot) / total)
            )
        masses = [sum(row[index] for row in responsibilities) for index in (0, 1)]
        if min(masses) < 1e-6:
            return float("-inf")
        new_weights = [mass / n for mass in masses]
        new_means = [
            sum(row[index] * value for row, value in zip(responsibilities, vals)) / masses[index]
            for index in (0, 1)
        ]
        new_variances = [
            max(
                sum(
                    row[index] * (value - new_means[index]) ** 2
                    for row, value in zip(responsibilities, vals)
                )
                / masses[index],
                floor,
            )
            for index in (0, 1)
        ]
        weights, means, variances = new_weights, new_means, new_variances
        if abs(next_loglike - loglike_two) < 1e-10:
            loglike_two = next_loglike
            break
        loglike_two = next_loglike
    bic_one = 2 * math.log(n) - 2.0 * loglike_one
    bic_two = 5 * math.log(n) - 2.0 * loglike_two
    return bic_one - bic_two


def modality_result(
    values: Sequence[float | int],
    *,
    discrete: bool,
    absolute_resolution: float,
    tier2: bool,
) -> ModalityResult:
    vals = sorted(_values(values))
    if len(vals) < 4:
        return ModalityResult(False, False, False, False, None, None, None)
    if discrete:
        counts: dict[float, int] = {}
        for value in vals:
            counts[value] = counts.get(value, 0) + 1
        distinct = sorted(counts)
        if len(distinct) < 2:
            return ModalityResult(False, False, False, False, None, None, None)
        recurrent = [value for value in distinct if counts[value] >= 2]
        flagged = len(recurrent) >= 2
        outlier = not flagged
        certified = tier2 and len([v for v in distinct if counts[v] >= 3]) >= 2
        return ModalityResult(
            flagged,
            outlier,
            certified,
            flagged and not certified,
            None,
            max(distinct) - min(distinct),
            "discrete_support" if flagged else "single_support_value",
        )

    gaps = [right - left for left, right in zip(vals, vals[1:])]
    largest_index = max(range(len(gaps)), key=gaps.__getitem__)
    largest = gaps[largest_index]
    left = vals[: largest_index + 1]
    right = vals[largest_index + 1 :]
    if len(left) == 1 or len(right) == 1:
        return ModalityResult(False, True, False, False, largest_index + 1, largest, "single_support_split")
    left_sd = statistics.stdev(left) if len(left) > 1 else 0.0
    right_sd = statistics.stdev(right) if len(right) > 1 else 0.0
    second = sorted(gaps, reverse=True)[1] if len(gaps) > 1 else 0.0
    mean = abs(statistics.fmean(vals))
    flagged = (
        largest >= 4.0 * max(left_sd, right_sd, absolute_resolution)
        and (mean == 0 or largest / mean >= 0.005)
        and (second == 0 or largest >= 2.5 * second)
    )
    support3 = len(left) >= 3 and len(right) >= 3
    delta_bic = (
        _continuous_delta_bic(vals, largest_index + 1, absolute_resolution)
        if flagged and tier2 and support3
        else float("-inf")
    )
    certified = flagged and tier2 and support3 and delta_bic > 6.0
    reason = None
    if flagged:
        reason = (
            "continuous_largest_gap_delta_bic"
            if certified
            else "continuous_largest_gap"
        )
    return ModalityResult(
        flagged,
        False,
        certified,
        flagged and not certified,
        largest_index + 1,
        largest,
        reason,
    )


def trigger_codes(
    values: Sequence[float | int],
    *,
    rule: str,
    absolute_resolution: float,
    discrete: bool,
    any_out_of_range: bool,
) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    vals = _values(values)
    codes: set[str] = set()
    modality = modality_result(
        vals,
        discrete=discrete,
        absolute_resolution=absolute_resolution,
        tier2=False,
    )
    if modality.flagged:
        codes.add("modality_flag")
    if modality.outlier_flag:
        codes.add("single_point_outlier")
    rel = sigma_rel(rule, vals, absolute_resolution=absolute_resolution)
    if rel is not None and rel > 0:
        if any(boundary / 2.0 <= rel <= boundary * 2.0 for boundary in CLASS_BOUNDARIES):
            codes.add("boundary_proximity")
    if any_out_of_range:
        codes.add("out_of_range")
    if discrete and len(set(vals)) >= 2:
        codes.add("discrete_multiple_values")
    return tuple(sorted(codes))


def percentile(values: Sequence[float], q: float) -> float:
    vals = sorted(_values(values))
    if not vals:
        raise DispersionError("percentile requires values")
    if not 0.0 <= q <= 1.0:
        raise DispersionError("percentile q outside [0,1]")
    position = (len(vals) - 1) * q
    lower = math.floor(position)
    upper = math.ceil(position)
    if lower == upper:
        return vals[lower]
    weight = position - lower
    return vals[lower] * (1.0 - weight) + vals[upper] * weight


def pooled_p90_upper(
    values: Sequence[float], *, seed: int, replicates: int = 1000
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    vals = _values(values)
    if not vals:
        raise DispersionError("pooled floor requires values")
    if isinstance(seed, bool) or not isinstance(seed, int):
        raise DispersionError("bootstrap seed must be an integer")
    if isinstance(replicates, bool) or not isinstance(replicates, int) or replicates < 1:
        raise DispersionError("bootstrap replicates must be positive")
    p90 = percentile(vals, 0.90)
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    boot = [
        percentile([vals[rng.randrange(len(vals))] for _ in vals], 0.90)
        for _ in range(replicates)
    ]
    return p90, percentile(boot, 0.90)


def median_bootstrap_ci(
    values: Sequence[float], *, seed: int, replicates: int = 1000
) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
    vals = _values(values)
    if not vals:
        raise DispersionError("median CI requires values")
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    boot = [
        statistics.median(vals[rng.randrange(len(vals))] for _ in vals)
        for _ in range(replicates)
    ]
    return statistics.median(vals), percentile(boot, 0.025), percentile(boot, 0.975)
```

```python
class StrictOntologyParserTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Negative cases for the strict registry_version>=2 ontology parser.

    Each case builds a minimal in-memory registry (registry_version 2), writes
    it to a temp file, and asserts load_registry rejects it with
    MetricRegistryError. A control case (a complete v2 registry) must load.
    """

    def setUp(self) -> None:
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        # Cache misses on path => give each registry a distinct path.
        self._counter = 0

    def tearDown(self) -> None:
        shutil.rmtree(self._tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)

    def _write(self, registry: dict) -> str:
        self._counter += 1
        path = Path(self._tmpdir) / f"reg_{self._counter}.json"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(registry), encoding="utf-8")
        return str(path)

    def _obs_contract(self) -> dict:
        return {
            "counting_unit": "L1TEX",
            "rollup": "sum",
            "numerator": "l1tex__t_requests_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld",
            "denominator": None,
            "op_classes": ["global_load"],
            "unsupported_op_behavior": (
                "kUnspecified->unsupported_memory_path typed fallback"
            ),
        }

    def _per_arch(self) -> dict:
        return {"sm_86": "available", "sm_120": "sm_120_deferred_no_live_evidence"}

    def _count_entry(self, **overrides) -> dict:
        entry = {

            "valid_max": None,
            "parser_transform": "identity_nonneg",

    def test_registry_versions_require_exact_json_integers(self) -> None:
        control = self._registry([self._count_entry()])
        for field, bad_value in (
            ("registry_version", True),
            ("registry_version", "2"),
            ("registry_version", 2.0),
            ("registry_version", 0),
            ("registry_version", 3),
            ("label_schema_version", False),
            ("label_schema_version", "5"),
            ("label_schema_version", 5.0),
        ):
            with self.subTest(field=field, bad_value=bad_value):
                invalid = copy.deepcopy(control)
                invalid[field] = bad_value
                with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
                    parse_registry(invalid)

    def test_registry_numeric_authorities_reject_coercions_and_nonfinite(self) -> None:
        control = self._registry([self._count_entry()])
        for bad_value in (True, "0.05", float("nan"), float("inf"), 10**400):
            with self.subTest(surface="threshold", bad_value=bad_value):
                invalid = copy.deepcopy(control)
                invalid["repeatability_thresholds"]["relative_tolerance"] = (
                    bad_value
                )
                with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
                    parse_registry(invalid)
            for field in ("valid_min", "valid_max"):
                with self.subTest(field=field, bad_value=bad_value):
                    invalid = copy.deepcopy(control)
                    invalid["metrics"][0][field] = bad_value
                    with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
                        parse_registry(invalid)

    def test_registry_nullable_requires_exact_json_boolean(self) -> None:
        control = self._registry([self._count_entry()])
        for bad_value in (0, 1, "false", None):
            with self.subTest(bad_value=bad_value):
                invalid = copy.deepcopy(control)
                invalid["metrics"][0]["nullable"] = bad_value
                with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
                    parse_registry(invalid)

    def test_registry_valid_range_must_be_ordered(self) -> None:
        invalid = self._registry([
            self._count_entry(valid_min=2.0, valid_max=1.0),
        ])
        with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
            parse_registry(invalid)

    def test_v2_rejects_entry_missing_metric_class(self) -> None:
        entry = self._count_entry()
        del entry["metric_class"]
        with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):
            load_registry(self._write(self._registry([entry])))

    def test_v2_rejects_entry_missing_risk_tier(self) -> None:

        with self.assertRaises(MetricRegistryError):

    def test_v2_rejects_entry_missing_ncu_observation_contract(self) -> None:

    def test_v2_rejects_observation_contract_missing_subkey(self) -> None:

    def test_v2_rejects_entry_missing_per_arch_availability(self) -> None:

    def test_v2_rejects_per_arch_availability_missing_arch(self) -> None:

    def test_v2_rejects_derived_entry_missing_composition(self) -> None:

    def test_pre_v2_keeps_ontology_fields_optional(self) -> None:

        # ontology fields, and still loads.
        entry = self._count_entry()

            "metric_class",

class NoLabelLeakageGuardTest(unittest.TestCase):
```

### E744 | sources: static-registry-projection | supports: B702
<!-- FABLE5-EVIDENCE
{"excerpt_sha256":"ce6c528b03b9664fce91cfca53773957867318ce4c7a7d8a3cb7419e8cc8866e","file_sha256":"ce6c528b03b9664fce91cfca53773957867318ce4c7a7d8a3cb7419e8cc8866e","file_total_lines":503,"final_newline":true,"full_required_justification":"Parsing, dependency ordering, cycle checks, formula evaluation, constants, status propagation, and result construction are distributed throughout this compact resolver.","id":"E744","kind":"file_full","lines":[1,503],"non_operational":true,"path":"tools/local_labels/composition_dag.py","revision":"WORKTREE","role":"decision","selection_reason":"The complete composition resolver exposes how declared dependencies, formulas, device constants, availability, and result domains are actually resolved, including the path by which prose-marked inexact SOL proxies can become resolved values.","supports":["B702"]}

```python
"""Composition DAG resolver over the registry's derived metrics.

A derived registry entry (``metric_class`` in ``derived_ratio`` /
``derived_pct_peak``) carries a ``composition`` block:

    {"formula": <str>,
     "dependencies": [<registry metric keys>],
     "device_constants": [<device-constant names>]}

The formula is an arithmetic expression whose bare identifiers are exactly the
dependency metric keys and the device-constant names. A dependency key may be a
PRIMITIVE (any non-derived registry metric, supplied at resolve time) or
ANOTHER derived metric (composition-of-composition); the latter forms an edge in
the dependency DAG so a derived metric is always evaluated after the derived
metrics it consumes.

This module builds that DAG, gives a topological evaluation order (raising on a
cycle), and evaluates each derived metric with a RESTRICTED ``ast`` evaluator
(no ``eval``/``exec``): only an arithmetic-expression node allowlist is honored,
device-constant names are resolved through the fail-closed
``DeviceConstantTable``, and an unavailable dependency cascades the derived value
to a typed-unavailable result with the offending dependency named.

Public surface:

- ``CompositionDAGResolver(registry, device_constant_table)``
  - ``.topological_order(arch) -> list[str]``
  - ``.resolve(arch, primitive_values) -> dict[key -> result dict]``
  - ``.refuse_label_leakage(feature_keys) -> None``
- ``CompositionError`` raised with a typed reason on a structural failure.

A ``resolve`` result for a derived key is
``{"value": float|None, "status": <str>, "reason": <str>}``; ``status`` is
``"resolved"`` when the formula produced a value, otherwise
``"typed_unavailable"`` with a ``reason`` that names the cause.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import ast
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Callable

from device_constants import DeviceConstantError, DeviceConstantTable
from metric_registry import MetricEntry, MetricRegistry

# Metric classes that carry a composition block and participate in the DAG.
DERIVED_METRIC_CLASSES: tuple[str, ...] = ("derived_ratio", "derived_pct_peak")

# Only explicitly available upstream dependencies can supply a value to a
# composition. Every other status, including sm_120_deferred_no_live_evidence,
# fails closed as a typed-unavailable dependency.
AVAILABLE_ARCH_STATUSES: frozenset[str] = frozenset({"available"})

# The only callables an allowlisted formula may invoke. These are pure,
# side-effect-free numeric reductions; NEVER expose builtins, attribute access,
# subscripting, comprehensions, or any name resolution outside this map.
_ALLOWED_CALLS: dict[str, Callable[..., float]] = {
    "min": min,
    "max": max,
    "abs": abs,
}

# Allowlisted ast node types for a formula. Anything outside this set is a
# rejected formula (composition_formula_unsafe). Note we deliberately exclude
# Attribute, Subscript, comprehensions, lambdas, BoolOp, Compare, IfExp, etc.
_ALLOWED_NODES: tuple[type, ...] = (
    ast.Expression,
    ast.BinOp,
    ast.UnaryOp,
    ast.Name,
    ast.Load,
    ast.Call,
    # Arithmetic operators.
    ast.Add,
    ast.Sub,
    ast.Mult,
    ast.Div,
    ast.Pow,
    ast.Mod,
    ast.UAdd,
    ast.USub,
)
# Numeric literals are ast.Constant on every supported Python (3.8+). The
# legacy ast.Num alias is deprecated (removed in 3.14) and is intentionally
# not referenced, so merely importing this module emits no DeprecationWarning.
_CONSTANT_NODES: tuple[type, ...] = (ast.Constant,)


class CompositionError(ValueError):
    """Raised on a structural composition failure with a typed reason.

    ``reason`` is one of:
      - ``composition_dag_cyclic``
      - ``composition_unknown_symbol``
      - ``device_constant_missing``
      - ``composition_formula_unsafe``
      - ``composition_formula_syntax``
      - ``composition_not_derived``
    """

    def __init__(self, reason: str, detail: str = "") -> None:
        self.reason = reason
        self.detail = detail
        message = reason if not detail else f"{reason}: {detail}"
        super().__init__(message)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class _DerivedNode:
    """One derived-metric node in the composition DAG."""

    key: str
    entry: MetricEntry
    formula: str
    dependencies: tuple[str, ...]
    device_constants: tuple[str, ...]

    @property
    def asserts_composition(self) -> bool:
        """True when the entry asserts a predictor-side composition from
        registered primitives. A derived entry that names NO dependencies and
        NO device constants carries a sentinel ``formula`` (e.g.
        ``label_only_no_predictor_composition`` /
        ``speed_of_light_requires_downstream_calibration``) recording that no
        composition from registered primitives is asserted; such a node is not
        evaluable here and resolves typed-unavailable rather than being parsed
        as an arithmetic formula."""
        return bool(self.dependencies) or bool(self.device_constants)


def _is_derived(entry: MetricEntry) -> bool:
    return entry.metric_class in DERIVED_METRIC_CLASSES


def _check_node_allowlist(tree: ast.AST) -> None:
    """Walk the parsed formula and reject any node outside the allowlist."""
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        if isinstance(node, _CONSTANT_NODES):
            # A constant must be numeric (int/float); reject str/bytes/None/bool.
            # Use ast.Constant.value (3.8+); avoid the deprecated .n alias.
            value = node.value if hasattr(node, "value") else node.n
            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
                raise CompositionError(
                    "composition_formula_unsafe",
                    f"non-numeric constant {value!r} in formula",
                )
            continue
        if isinstance(node, _ALLOWED_NODES):
            if isinstance(node, ast.Call):
                # Only a bare-name call to an allowlisted reduction, no kwargs,
                # no starred args.
                if not isinstance(node.func, ast.Name):
                    raise CompositionError(
                        "composition_formula_unsafe",
                        "only direct calls to allowlisted functions are permitted",
                    )
                if node.func.id not in _ALLOWED_CALLS:
                    raise CompositionError(
                        "composition_formula_unsafe",
                        f"call to non-allowlisted function {node.func.id!r}",
                    )
                if node.keywords:
                    raise CompositionError(
                        "composition_formula_unsafe",
                        "keyword arguments are not permitted in formula calls",
                    )
                for arg in node.args:
                    if isinstance(arg, ast.Starred):
                        raise CompositionError(
                            "composition_formula_unsafe",
                            "starred arguments are not permitted in formula calls",
                        )
            continue
        raise CompositionError(
            "composition_formula_unsafe",
            f"disallowed expression node {type(node).__name__}",
        )


def _parse_formula(formula: str) -> ast.Expression:
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(formula, mode="eval")
    except SyntaxError as exc:
        raise CompositionError(
            "composition_formula_syntax", f"{formula!r}: {exc}"
        ) from exc
    _check_node_allowlist(tree)
    return tree


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CompositionDAGResolver:
    """Builds and evaluates the DAG over the registry's derived metrics."""

    registry: MetricRegistry
    device_constant_table: DeviceConstantTable

    # ----- DAG construction ------------------------------------------------

    def _entry_by_key(self) -> dict[str, MetricEntry]:
        return {e.key: e for e in self.registry.entries}

    def _derived_nodes(self) -> dict[str, _DerivedNode]:
        by_key = self._entry_by_key()
        nodes: dict[str, _DerivedNode] = {}
        for entry in self.registry.entries:
            if not _is_derived(entry):
                continue
            comp = entry.composition or {}
            deps = tuple(comp.get("dependencies", []) or ())
            consts = tuple(comp.get("device_constants", []) or ())
            formula = comp.get("formula", "")
            nodes[entry.key] = _DerivedNode(
                key=entry.key,
                entry=entry,
                formula=str(formula),
                dependencies=deps,
                device_constants=consts,
            )
        # Sanity: every derived dependency that is itself derived must be a
        # known node (a derived dep referencing a missing/unknown key is an
        # unknown symbol; that surfaces during evaluation, but a derived->derived
        # edge to a non-existent key would otherwise silently drop, so we only
        # build edges to keys that exist in the registry).
        del by_key
        return nodes

    def _derived_edges(
        self, nodes: dict[str, _DerivedNode]
    ) -> dict[str, set[str]]:
        """Edge map node -> set of derived dependency nodes it consumes.

        Only dependencies that are themselves derived metrics (present in
        ``nodes``) create ordering edges; primitive dependencies are leaves.
        """
        edges: dict[str, set[str]] = {k: set() for k in nodes}
        for key, node in nodes.items():
            for dep in node.dependencies:
                if dep in nodes:
                    edges[key].add(dep)
        return edges

    def _validate_dependency_keys(self, nodes: dict[str, _DerivedNode]) -> None:
        """Every declared dependency must be a registered metric key."""
        by_key = self._entry_by_key()
        for node in nodes.values():
            for dep in node.dependencies:
                if dep not in by_key:
                    raise CompositionError(
                        "composition_unknown_symbol",
                        f"{node.key} dependency {dep!r} is not a registry key",
                    )

    @staticmethod
    def _arch_status(per_arch: dict[str, Any], arch: str) -> str | None:
        status = per_arch.get(arch)
        if isinstance(status, dict):
            raw = status.get("status")
            return str(raw) if raw is not None else None
        return str(status) if status is not None else None

    def topological_order(self, arch: str) -> list[str]:
        """Return derived-metric keys ordered so every metric follows the
        derived metrics it depends on. Raises ``CompositionError`` with reason
        ``composition_dag_cyclic`` on a dependency cycle.

        ``arch`` is accepted for interface symmetry with ``resolve``; the
        derived-metric topology is architecture-independent (the device-constant
        table only affects evaluable VALUES, not the dependency structure).
        """
        del arch  # topology does not depend on arch; kept for a uniform API.
        nodes = self._derived_nodes()
        self._validate_dependency_keys(nodes)
        edges = self._derived_edges(nodes)
        # Kahn's algorithm over edges (dep -> dependent) reversed: we have
        # edges[node] = its derived deps. Process a node only after all its
        # derived deps are emitted.
        emitted: list[str] = []
        emitted_set: set[str] = set()
        remaining = dict(edges)
        # Deterministic order: sort keys so the output is stable.
        progress = True
        while remaining and progress:
            progress = False
            for key in sorted(remaining):
                if remaining[key] <= emitted_set:
                    emitted.append(key)
                    emitted_set.add(key)
                    del remaining[key]
                    progress = True
        if remaining:
            cyclic = ", ".join(sorted(remaining))
            raise CompositionError(
                "composition_dag_cyclic",
                f"derived metrics form a dependency cycle: {cyclic}",
            )
        return emitted

    # ----- Evaluation ------------------------------------------------------

    def _dep_unavailable_reason(
        self,
        arch: str,
        node: _DerivedNode,
        primitive_values: dict[str, float],
        resolved: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> str | None:
        """If any dependency of ``node`` cannot supply a value on ``arch``,
        return a ``dependency_unavailable:<dep>`` reason for the first such
        dependency; otherwise ``None``."""
        by_key = self._entry_by_key()
        for dep in node.dependencies:
            dep_entry = by_key.get(dep)
            if dep_entry is None:
                # Unknown dependency key: not a value problem, an unknown symbol.
                # Surfaced at evaluation time via the symbol allowlist.
                continue
            # Per-arch availability gate on the dependency.
            per_arch = dep_entry.per_arch_availability or {}
            status = self._arch_status(per_arch, arch)
            if status not in AVAILABLE_ARCH_STATUSES:
                return f"dependency_unavailable:{dep}"
            if _is_derived(dep_entry):
                # A derived dependency must have resolved to a value already.
                dep_result = resolved.get(dep)
                if dep_result is None or dep_result.get("value") is None:
                    return f"dependency_unavailable:{dep}"
            else:
                # A primitive dependency must be supplied (and non-None).
                if dep not in primitive_values or primitive_values[dep] is None:
                    return f"dependency_unavailable:{dep}"
        return None

    def _build_environment(
        self,
        arch: str,
        node: _DerivedNode,
        primitive_values: dict[str, float],
        resolved: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    ) -> dict[str, float]:
        """Resolve every symbol the formula may reference into a numeric value:
        dependency metric keys (from primitives or previously-resolved derived)
        and device-constant names (from the fail-closed table)."""
        by_key = self._entry_by_key()
        env: dict[str, float] = {}
        for dep in node.dependencies:
            dep_entry = by_key.get(dep)
            if dep_entry is not None and _is_derived(dep_entry):
                env[dep] = float(resolved[dep]["value"])
            else:
                env[dep] = float(primitive_values[dep])
        for const_name in node.device_constants:
            try:
                env[const_name] = self.device_constant_table.get(arch, const_name)
            except DeviceConstantError as exc:
                raise CompositionError(
                    "device_constant_missing", f"{const_name} (arch {arch}): {exc}"
                ) from exc
        return env

    def _eval_node(self, ast_node: ast.AST, env: dict[str, float]) -> float:
        """Evaluate an allowlisted ast node against ``env`` (no eval/exec)."""
        if isinstance(ast_node, ast.Expression):
            return self._eval_node(ast_node.body, env)
        if isinstance(ast_node, _CONSTANT_NODES):
            # ast.Constant.value on modern Python (3.8+); avoid the deprecated
            # .n alias so no DeprecationWarning fires on the hot eval path.
            raw = ast_node.value if hasattr(ast_node, "value") else ast_node.n
            return float(raw)
        if isinstance(ast_node, ast.Name):
            try:
                return float(env[ast_node.id])
            except KeyError as exc:
                raise CompositionError(
                    "composition_unknown_symbol", ast_node.id
                ) from exc
        if isinstance(ast_node, ast.UnaryOp):
            operand = self._eval_node(ast_node.operand, env)
            if isinstance(ast_node.op, ast.UAdd):
                return +operand
            if isinstance(ast_node.op, ast.USub):
                return -operand
            raise CompositionError(
                "composition_formula_unsafe",
                f"unary op {type(ast_node.op).__name__}",
            )
        if isinstance(ast_node, ast.BinOp):
            left = self._eval_node(ast_node.left, env)
            right = self._eval_node(ast_node.right, env)
            op = ast_node.op
            if isinstance(op, ast.Add):
                return left + right
            if isinstance(op, ast.Sub):
                return left - right
            if isinstance(op, ast.Mult):
                return left * right
            if isinstance(op, ast.Div):
                return left / right
            if isinstance(op, ast.Pow):
                return left ** right
            if isinstance(op, ast.Mod):
                return left % right
            raise CompositionError(
                "composition_formula_unsafe",
                f"binary op {type(op).__name__}",
            )
        if isinstance(ast_node, ast.Call):
            func = ast_node.func
            if not isinstance(func, ast.Name) or func.id not in _ALLOWED_CALLS:
                raise CompositionError(
                    "composition_formula_unsafe", "non-allowlisted call"
                )
            args = [self._eval_node(a, env) for a in ast_node.args]
            return float(_ALLOWED_CALLS[func.id](*args))
        raise CompositionError(
            "composition_formula_unsafe",
            f"disallowed node {type(ast_node).__name__}",
        )

    def _validate_symbols(self, node: _DerivedNode, tree: ast.Expression) -> None:
        """Every Name in the formula must be a declared dependency key or a
        declared device-constant name; otherwise composition_unknown_symbol."""
        known = set(node.dependencies) | set(node.device_constants)
        for sub in ast.walk(tree):
            if isinstance(sub, ast.Call) and isinstance(sub.func, ast.Name):
                # Function names (min/max/abs) are not data symbols.
                continue
            if isinstance(sub, ast.Name):
                if sub.id in _ALLOWED_CALLS:
                    continue
                if sub.id not in known:
                    raise CompositionError("composition_unknown_symbol", sub.id)

    def resolve(
        self, arch: str, primitive_values: dict[str, float]
    ) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
        """Evaluate every derived metric for ``arch`` in topological order.

        ``primitive_values`` maps PRIMITIVE (non-derived) registry metric keys to
        their numeric values. For each derived metric the result is
        ``{"value": float|None, "status": str, "reason": str}``:

          - a metric whose every dependency is available and whose formula
            evaluates returns ``{"value": <float>, "status": "resolved",
            "reason": ""}``;
          - a metric with an unavailable dependency (per-arch status other than
            available, or a primitive missing
            from ``primitive_values``, or an upstream derived that itself did not
            resolve) cascades to ``{"value": None, "status":
            "typed_unavailable", "reason": "dependency_unavailable:<dep>"}``.

        Structural formula failures (unknown symbol, missing device constant,
        unsafe/cyclic formula) raise ``CompositionError`` — they are author-time
        registry defects, not per-run unavailability.
        """
        order = self.topological_order(arch)
        nodes = self._derived_nodes()
        resolved: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
        for key in order:
            node = nodes[key]
            if not node.asserts_composition:
                # A derived entry that asserts no composition from registered
                # primitives (no dependencies, no device constants) is not
                # evaluable here; its sentinel formula is a marker, not an
                # arithmetic expression. Resolve typed-unavailable, fail-closed,
                # rather than parsing the sentinel.
                resolved[key] = {
                    "value": None,
                    "status": "typed_unavailable",
                    "reason": "no_predictor_composition",
                }
                continue
            tree = _parse_formula(node.formula)
            # Symbol-allowlist check is a structural property of the formula and
            # is enforced even when a dependency is unavailable, so an authoring
            # typo never hides behind a cascade.
            self._validate_symbols(node, tree)
            unavailable = self._dep_unavailable_reason(
                arch, node, primitive_values, resolved
            )
            if unavailable is not None:
                resolved[key] = {
                    "value": None,
                    "status": "typed_unavailable",
                    "reason": unavailable,
                }
                continue
            env = self._build_environment(arch, node, primitive_values, resolved)
            value = self._eval_node(tree, env)
            resolved[key] = {
                "value": float(value),
                "status": "resolved",
                "reason": "",
            }
        return resolved

    # ----- Guards ----------------------------------------------------------

    def refuse_label_leakage(self, feature_keys: set[str]) -> None:
        """Delegate to the registry's no-NCU-label-leakage guard. Fail closed if
        any feature key resolves to a ``label_only`` registry entry."""
        self.registry.assert_no_label_leakage(feature_keys)
```
